title: Prime-to-characteristic torsion is dense in an abelian variety
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $B/F$ be an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety]. For each integer $n\geq1$ whose image in $F$ is nonzero, let $B[n]$ be the kernel of multiplication by $n$ [def-sc-mult-n]. The subset $T=\bigcup_{n\geq1,\,n\in F^\times}B[n](F)$ of rational points [def-pc-rational-point] is Zariski dense in $B$: every closed subset of the underlying topological space of $B$ containing all the images of the points in $T$ is the whole space. The assertion includes the zero-dimensional abelian variety.

source.place: I Section 10, pp.42–45 (torsion and isogenies); the explicit density statement and proof are the first unnumbered lemma after Proposition 12.1 in Milne, Abelian Varieties, January 2, 2022, Section 12, printed p.19, https://www.jmilne.org/math/xnotes/AVs.pdf. The latter article is WANTED; see report.md. Agent supporting lemma, not a claim that the local PDF states it verbatim.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-av-commutative], $B(F)$ is abelian. The set $T$ is a subgroup: $0\in B[1](F)$; if $nx=0$ and $my=0$ with $n,m$ invertible in $F$, then $nm(x-y)=0$ and $nm$ is invertible. Form $P=\coprod_{t\in T}\operatorname{Spec}F$ using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], and the constant-group multiplication of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-group-scheme-multiplication]. Its unit is the inclusion labelled $0$, and its inverse carries the copy labelled $t$ identically to the copy labelled $-t$. The group axioms follow on each open component from the corresponding equalities in $T$. The coproduct universal property gives $a:P\to B$ restricting to the rational point $t$ on the copy labelled $t$. On every component labelled $(t,u)$ of $P\times_F P$, compatibility with addition is the equality $t+u=t+u$ in $B(F)$; unit and inverse compatibility are identical. Thus $a$ is a group-scheme homomorphism, and its topological image is exactly the set of images of the points of $T$.

source.place: Lemma 1.40 and Definition 1.48, pp.18–20; explicit constant-group evaluation construction.

proof.text: Regard $P$ and $B$ as absolute groupoids with object scheme $\operatorname{Spec}F$: both source and target are their structure map, composition is addition, and their unit and inverse are the group operations [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. The map $a$ of step 1 commutes with these operations. The field $F$ is perfect: in characteristic $p>0$, each $c\in F$ has a root of $X^p-c$, and characteristic-zero fields are perfect. Apply [lem-sfb-perfect-field-groupoid-image-closure] to $a$. It gives the reduced closed subgroup scheme $H\hookrightarrow B$ with underlying subset $\overline T$. This application allows the infinite coproduct $P$: the cited statement has no finite-type or quasi-compactness hypothesis on the source. The scheme $H$ is of finite type over $F$: on each member $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of a finite affine cover of $B$, its intersection is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$, and the quotient of a finitely generated $F$-algebra is finitely generated [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Tag 04Q8, lemma-map-groupoids-on-perfect-field-image, applied to the evaluation homomorphism from a constant group scheme.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-abelian-closed-subgroup-reduced-component] to $H\hookrightarrow B$. Since $H$ is reduced, its identity component $C=H^0$ is an abelian variety and a closed subgroup of $B$. By [lem-sfb-group-neutral-component-translates], $H$ has finitely many components, each a rational translate of $C$; denote their number by $r\geq1$. By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], write $g=\dim B$ and $h=\dim C$ as nonnegative integers; both schemes contain the identity. Dimensions here mean the chain dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], which is the $\kundim$ of the finiteness lemma. Since $C$ is a closed subset of $B$, any chain in $C$ is also a chain in $B$, so $h\leq g$.

source.place: Proposition 1.34, Corollary 1.35 and dimension discussion before Proposition 1.37, pp.16–18; Milne AV I Proposition 8.1, p.35.

proof.text: Fix a prime $\ell$ invertible in $F$ (take $2$ unless $\operatorname{char}F=2$, in which case take $3$). For every $m\geq1$, put $N=\ell^m$. Apply [lem-sc-ntorsion-etale] to $B$ and to $C$ ($N$ is prime to $\operatorname{char}F$): $B[N](F)\cong(\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z)^{2g}$ and $C[N](F)\cong(\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z)^{2h}$, so $\#B[N](F)=N^{2g}$ and $\#C[N](F)=N^{2h}$. Every point of $B[N](F)$ belongs to $T\subseteq H(F)$. In any one component of $H$, either there is no such point, or choose one, $x$. Subtracting $x$ injects the $N$-torsion points of that component into $C[N](F)$: translation identifies the component with $C$ by step 3, and $N(y-x)=Ny-Nx=0$. Thus each of the $r$ components contains at most $N^{2h}$ of these points, and $N^{2g}\leq rN^{2h}$.

source.place: Theorem 7.2 and Remark 7.3, pp.33–34, prime-to-characteristic torsion count; componentwise subtraction argument supplied here.

proof.text: If $h<g$, cancelling the positive integer $N^{2h}$ in the inequality of step 4 gives $\ell^{2m(g-h)}\leq r$ for every $m\geq1$. Taking $m=r+1$ contradicts this, since $\ell\geq2$ and $g-h\geq1$ give $\ell^{2m(g-h)}\geq2^m\geq m+1>r$ (the inequality $2^m\geq m+1$ follows by induction). Hence $h=g$.

source.place: Agent counting argument from Theorem 7.2 and Remark 7.3; no density theorem used.

proof.text: The variety $B$ is irreducible by [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization]. If the closed subset $C\subseteq B$ were proper, a chain of irreducible closed subsets of length $h=g$ in $C$ would extend by appending $B$, giving a chain of length $g+1$ in $B$. Such a chain in $C$ exists because its finite integer dimension is the supremum of the integer chain lengths [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. This contradicts $\dim B=g$. Thus $|C|=|B|$, so $|B|=|C|\subseteq|H|=\overline T\subseteq|B|$. Every closed subset containing $T$ contains its closure, and is therefore all of $|B|$. The argument also covers $g=0$: $h\leq g$ forces $h=g=0$, and the same chain argument shows $C=B$.

source.place: Corollary 1.35, p.17; final dimension comparison written directly from the definition of chain dimension.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 7.2 and Remark 7.3 (pp.33–34), with Milne iAG2017 1.34–1.48 and Stacks Tag 04Q8; explicit torsion-counting density argument. The 2022 Section 12 density lemma remains WANTED.

Step 2 applies Stacks 04Q8 (more-groupoids.tex l.1563; its Situation imposes no finiteness on R_1, so the infinite P is allowed; F algebraically closed is perfect).
